instruction: Export the current webpage to PDF and store it on the Desktop using the default name.

metadata.explanation: Task requires saving the webpage as PDF to Desktop. Evaluator verifies that the PDF file exists at the expected location and contains at least 1 page. Uses custom getter to extract PDF metadata (exists, page_count, file_size) and custom metric to verify file existence and minimum page count.
metadata.verification_details: Verified that PDF file path matches Chrome's default naming pattern for the webpage title. Minimum page count set to 1 as the webpage contains substantial content that will generate at least one PDF page.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: (1) PDF saved, (2) to Desktop location, (3) with default filename
Getter logic is correct: retrieves PDF file from VM, parses with pypdf, extracts existence and page count
Metric logic is correct: verifies file exists and contains at least 1 page (reasonable for webpage content)
Expected value is semantically correct: min_pages=1 is appropriate, filepath matches Chrome's default naming pattern for the webpage title
Data flow is correct: getter extracts {exists, page_count, file_size} -> metric checks exists and page_count >= min_pages
No postconfig needed: PDF file is persisted to disk, state is stable
Minor issue: Type annotation mismatch (getter returns Optional[Dict], metric expects Dict), but runtime-safe due to 'if not result' check at metric line 19
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional: Fix type annotation consistency - change getter return type from Optional[Dict] to Dict, or change metric parameter type to Optional[Dict]. Current code is runtime-safe but type annotations could be more precise.
